agree.reason: A household that felt ignored and shortchanged gets a plain apology, a weekly email, and a set credit rule for weather-cut boxes, which answers both complaints and makes signing up again a reasonable choice.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief and the limits are stated openly (greens not covered, no promise of a loss-free season), but 'Here's what we've done' presents two promises for the coming season as already done, and 'most of you' is used where '29 of 41' would be more exact.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only repeated: the email never says 29 of 41, never works out the weekly value of a $540 share (about $24.50) to show what the new credit is worth, and never shows what the old policy cost this reader over six half-boxes.

right_comparison.reason: The email sets last year's handling (no credit, one email) against this year's rules fairly, but it doesn't spell out the difference in money, or say what the reader would face from the same storm under each policy.

qualification.reason: The credit condition (weather cutting a box by more than a third) uses a number the reader can check and has a clear consequence, and the 'no promise of no crop loss' hedge is honest, though the email doesn't say how the credit is paid or when.

objections.reason: Both of the reader's grievances, the silence and the lack of a refund, are answered directly by the weekly email and the credit rule, and the email raises no objections the facts already settle; it doesn't address whether last year's loss will be made good in any way.

fit.reason: It is a short, personal email of about 190 words with a clear subject line and closing details, so it is under the 200-word limit and in the form the brief asked for.
